chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:

He عليه السلام said: “Indeed, from among us is an Imam, victorious and concealed. So when Allah, Mighty is His remembrance, intends to manifest His command, He impresses a mark into his heart; then he appears and rises by the command of Allah, Blessed and Exalted.”

key_terms.أَمْرِ اللَّهِ: the command and decree of Allah governing the Imam’s rise
key_terms.إِظْهَارَ: the bringing forth or manifesting of a matter by divine will
key_terms.إِمَامًا: a divinely designated leader from the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.النَّاقُورِ: the trumpet or horn whose sounding is invoked here in the Qur'anic phrase being interpreted
key_terms.مُسْتَتِرًا: concealed or hidden from public appearance
key_terms.مُظَفَّرًا: one granted victory or made triumphant
key_terms.نَكَتَ: He impressed or placed suddenly and decisively
key_terms.نُكْتَةً: a mark, indication, or decisive impression placed in the heart

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith explain the verse “Then when the trumpet is sounded” in relation to the concealed Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse as an indication of a concealed Imam from the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام whose emergence occurs by Allah’s command. It emphasizes that his appearance is divinely initiated and inwardly signaled, after which he rises to establish the command of Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
